Conflict situations have never been new to Kashmiri people or Kashmir valley. From the past 28 years, Kashmir Valley has been witnessing a protracted conflict resulting in a huge impact on the day to day lives of common Kashmiri people. The last bout of serious violence in the region was in the summer of 2010, when more than 100 people died in anti-India protests, which broke out after police shot dead a teenager.
The conflict resistant Kashmir and its people once again witnessed the paradise on fire because of the killing of Burhan Wani- Commander Hizbul Mujahedeen. This

, refers to a series of violent protests in the Muslim-majority Kashmir Valley in the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir. It started with the killing of Burhan Wani, a militant commander of the Kashmir-based Hizbul Mujahedeen along with his two associates by Indian security forces on 8 July 2016 in the Kokernag area. Burhan was popular among Kashmiri’s due to his activities on social media because of which after his killing, anti- Indian protests started in all districts of the Kashmir valley.

Curfew was imposed all over the valley following the suspension of mobile and internet services by the government. To control the riots, the Jammu and Kashmir Police and Para-military forces used Pellet Guns, Tear gas shells, Rubber bullets and also live ammunition on the protesters, resulting in the deaths, injuries and disabilities.

Security forces while trying to control the Kashmiri agitators used Pellet guns, which although billed as "non-lethal", lead to a high number of casualties including permanent eye injuries. When pellet cartridges bursts, hundreds of tiny metallic particles jet out and penetrate skin and eyes, rupturing them before

Due to the medical emergency in Kashmir, there was a shortage of eye specialists who could treat the injured lying in Kashmiri hospitals. In Shri Maharaja Hari Singh (SMHS) Hospital of Srinagar, over 200 patients are presently admitted with the same problem.

In response State Government sends a three-member team of eye-specialists from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences from New Delhi to help the local doctors in treating the pellet gun injuries. After watching the condition of patients in the hospital, they described the situation as a "war-like situation".

By 22 July, the SMHS Hospital has received at least 182 patients with eye injuries caused mostly due to pellets with more than 137 eye surgeries having taken place (DR. Tariq Qureshi, HOD ophthalmology dept. - SMHS)

Response of Borderless World Foundation towards 2016 unrest

Seeing the valley on once again facing severe crises, mourning the deaths of their beloved ones, Borderless World Foundation once again send out its local team headed by Sheikh Shahnawaz Zahoor, Chairman, BWF -JKL to access the reality of ground and realize the need of the hour. Mr. Zahoor formed a team of 4 Officials of BWF for field study.
Mr. Haris Abrar Kashmiri- Sr. Program officer BWF
Ms. Iqra Javed- Program Officer BWF
Ms. Gitanjali Das Gupta- Internee BWF from Pune
Before going on field a plan of strategy was formed as

On day first, as a team when everyone met after a long break it was somehow psychological first aid for each member as everyone was locked in homes due to curfew and nobody was having an access to mobile services and internet. There were some ideas on everyone’s mind gained through news channels that pellet injuries have increased, situation at hospitals are grim, patients facing insufficient medical assistance etc but the real scenario was felt by everyone after entering the SMHS Hospital. The scene was community kitchen (voluntary organization’s preparing food for patients) going on, panic, chaos, frustrated masses, depressed faces, cries, screams, sirens of ambulances were seen and heard all around.
As decided the team went into the wards of Eye pellet injuries, observing the situation.

Due to continuous increase in number of patients, two patients were placed on one bed. The attendees with the patients were crying in search of hope for their wards as they were complaining that no one is telling them the reality what has happened to their wards and is there any chance of Vision restoration.
The team decided to talk with some attendants and patients for more clarifications. We in team went to one patient and started giving introduction of the team and the overall motive behind the visit.

While doing so, we were surrounded with people and all of them were looking at us with suspicious eyes as they were informed that some agents from police are roaming. Meanwhile one small child of 15 or 16 year old cried out thought that we might be from media.
“You press people come here to listen to our woes but don’t report it. Please don’t do this, Kashmir is burning,”

Trying to build some rapo, the team started to answer the enquiries. It was felt that no one was giving us the correct information and majority of them was not interested to talk. The hopelessness and fear was visible on everyone’s face.
“Doctors came, put eye drops on our eyes and left, what has happened to us no one is answering” said Amir (name changed) a 17 year old boy.

Everyone was enquiring about the vision restoration whether that was patient or attendant. The people over there were frustrated and depressed so, respecting the individuality and willingness of people over there, the team left to meet Dr. Tariq Qureshi, H.O.D Ophthalmology Department- SMHS
Dr. Tariq showed great response and support towards the meeting. The following information was revealed
We saw in wards that the patients have operated once but they are not discharged yet?

The patients have operated once and the reason behind keeping them in hospital is that the pellet is still in their eye and doctors are not able to operate that due to non availability of Retina surgeon.
The patients who were having pellet in other sections of eye have been treated and discharged but the patients who are presently in wards are the one who have pellets in their Retina.
At present how many patients are such?

Presently, there are around 105 pellets injured in hospital out of which 70 are those who have retina injuries and needs to be treated immediately. On personal level we are trying to coordinate with outside hospitals for their surgeries but the number is very high and day by day it’s increasing.
What SMHS needs most at present which can help?
Presently we are facing non availability of some medicines, the list of the same can be provided to you and equipment called as Portable B-Scan is required which is used in surgeries.

The team of BWF thanked Dr. Qureshi for spending some time from his busy schedule and requested for one more meeting for discussing the possible way of intervention by BWF. The list of medicines was taken along and the report of the same was discussed with Mr. Zahoor- Chairman BWFJKL and head office Pune.

Through the meeting with Dr. Tariq Qureshi it was accessed that the immediate need of the hour was to cure the retina damages of pellet victims as some local NGOs and Voluntary groups were already working on the procurement of basic requirements like food and medicines.

The board members of BWF first decided of getting the patients flown out of Kashmir for better treatment but encountered logistical problems and the process seemed time consuming as it was not the matter of one surgery, there were plight of pellet victims which were in need of immediate help. After lot of overnight discussions and meetings, the plan of intervention was formed and it was decided to bring surgeon doctors to valley for conducting Retina surgeries.
But things don’t always turn up easy for NGOs. In all this action the support and trust of SMHS doctors and patients was required for which on 11

July, a meeting was held between Suhail Masoodi (Advisory BWF), Dr. Arshad, Dr. Sajad Khandey, Dr. Saleem -ur- Rehman along with some more dignitaries of health department. The meeting ends up on suggesting that only best services can heal the patients. The need of hour and minutes of meeting was shared by Suhail Masoodi with the board members of BWF- Pune comprising of Sheikh Shanawaz Zahoor- Chairman BWFJKL, the Founder of BWF- Mr. Adhik Kadam, Mr. Aslam and Dr. Rushikesh.

Not wasting much time Dr. Rushikesh, who acted as a coordinator for this program met Dr. S. Natrajan as he can be the only choice when thought of Retina surgeon comes in anyone’s mind. Dr. Natrajan was briefed about the situation of ground zero and the nature of the injuries. In response without any hesitation he agreed upon operating pellet victims and started coordinating with Dr. Rushikesh for the same cause.

Dr. Tariq Qureshi showed an immense support and welcomed our proposal of help and started coordinating for the same with Mr. Adhik Kadam, Founder-BWFJKL and Mr. Suhail Masoodi, Advisory-BWF in order to maintain the confidentiality of records of patients.
With lot of hard work and support from SMHS hospital especially Dr. Arshad, Dr. Sajad Khandey, Dr. Saleem-ur-rehman and
Borderless World Foundation was able to facilitate free Retinal Surgeries at SMHS Hospital, Srinagar.

A team of three eye-specialists arrived on 26 July all over from Mumbai to treat eye injuries caused by the pellets. The team was led by no doubt Padma Shri awarded, Madurai-born ophthalmologist, who is chairman-cum-managing director of Aditya Jyoti Eye Hospital, Mumbai, Internationally acclaimed vitreous retina specialist and
along with his team of two retina surgeons

The doctors were welcomed by Personal Assistant of Dr. Tariq Qureshi and BWF members. The doctors were accompanied with Dr. Rushikesh who is associated with BWF since its inception. After landing on Srinagar airport, without wasting any time all the doctors went to SMHS, meet patients in wards and start operating them.

As the news spread in the wards of SMHS that Dr. Natarajan along with a team of doctors has came to treat pellet victims, everyone was boosted with a ray of hope and the news imposed life to their dead emotions and trust for the doctors and BWF team was seen in everyone’s face and gestures. The response and trust of patients and attendees pumped the positive motivation in the atmosphere. The place which was shattered with hopelessness and anger was suddenly full of hopes and satisfaction and the arrival of doctors turned to be a healing touch.
With a deep breath, an attendant with one of the patient came to us and said,
“We are sorry as we thought you are here to make only story on us but you have come up with such a great help, May God bless you”.
